newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge higher on Dow in slow start.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge higher on Dow in slow start.

text.p: Mexican stocks chalked up modest gains Tuesday as trade resumed after a long holiday weekend in a cautious response to a rally posted Monday on Wall Street, traders said.
"They waited to see which way the Dow would go at first, and then a few buyers stepped in, but there are few investors right now. It's still quiet," a floor trader said.

The leading IPC share index was up 14.14 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.38 percent, at 3,779.02 points. Trading volume was restrained at 6.7 million shares, and included several cross trades, dealers said.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 19.26 points at 7,233.75.
"We're up a little on the Dow's coattails, but we don't expect much activity until mid-morning. The market is still a little slow after the long weekend," a desk trader said.
Mexican financial markets were closed on Monday to commemorate the anniversary of the battle of Puebla.
Dealers noted most blue chips were moderately ahead in early trade, but said volume was too thin to betoken any firm market trends.
Financial stock Bancomer, unchanged at 2.80 pesos, weighed most heavily on early trade, dealers said.
Cement maker Cemex weighed on the upside in relatively brisk trade, up 15 centavos to 26.50 pesos in what traders said was a technical rebound after suffering in recent sessions.
